subject: Tiered failover activated: NimbusTech hosted API impact and next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Redding <alex.redding@nimbustech.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tiered failover activated: NimbusTech hosted API impact and next steps

Hi Alex —

Quick heads-up: at 08:03 PT we detected a sustained spike in p99 generation latency for your account on our hosted inference fleet in us-west-1. The spike correlated with a sharp increase in KV cache eviction rates for the model family you’re using. To protect availability we activated our tiered failover policy and started routing matched traffic to a compatible variant running in us-east-1 and a quantized fallback in us-west-2.

What you may have seen: some requests experienced increased round-trip latency (~120–350ms additional p95) and a small subset of requests were served by the quantized fallback (slight tokenization differences, no truncation). No requests were dropped. We did not observe model output corruption, but answer timings were higher for a short window while routing converged.

What we did immediately:
- Triggered tiered failover to preserve availability.
- Throttled non-essential background batching on the affected shards.
- Captured KV eviction/daemon logs and snapshot (attached: kv-eviction-logs-0411.txt).
- Posted a live incident entry on our status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2027-04-11-nimbus-tiered-failover

Next steps from us:
- We’re keeping the tiered routing in place while we stabilize the affected pool (target: full revert to primary routing within 2 hours).
- Engineering is applying an autoscaler threshold hotfix and a KV cache tuning change; we’ll revert the routing once the metrics are stable for 30 minutes.
- We will produce a postmortem with mitigation and any recommended client-side changes within 72 hours.

Attachments: incident-graph-20270411.png (p99 trends), runbook-failover-snippet.pdf (excerpt used during activation).

Apologies for the disruption — I’ll update you as we have the revert time confirmed. Feel free to reply here or open the ticket id 76234 if you want a dedicated call.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Alex Redding <alex.redding@nimbustech.ai>

Date: 2027-04-11T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered failover activated: NimbusTech hosted API impact and next steps

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the quick action. A couple quick questions:

1) ETA on when traffic will be fully routed back to normal?
2) Were any completions truncated or materially altered by the quantized fallback? We run some strict QA checks on outputs, want to know if we need to replay any jobs.
3) Can you share the logs/trace ids that correspond to our API key so our engineers can correlate on our side?

If this looks like it will be >2 hours we’ll need to escalate to the platform team internally.

— Alex
Alex Redding
Platform Lead, NimbusTech
alex.redding@nimbustech.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Redding <alex.redding@nimbustech.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, support@nimbustech.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered failover activated: NimbusTech hosted API impact and next steps

Alex —

Short answers up front: we expect to revert primary routing within ~90 minutes pending metric stability; we have not seen truncation or malformed outputs in sampled traces but there are minor probability-shift differences when served by the quantized fallback.

More detail: preliminary root cause looks like a high-prefix churn event generated by a large onboarding job (not from NimbusTech) that produced an outsized KV cache eviction cascade on a small set of us-west shards. That eviction spike caused the autoscaler to mark capacity as degraded for several adjacent shards which then increased queuing latency. Tiered failover prevented client-visible errors but introduced higher latency where routing crossed regions or used a quantized variant.

What we’ve pushed:
- Short-term: autoscaler threshold rollback on affected host pool + KV cache LRU tuning (in flight).
- Medium-term: a guard to detect prefix-churn patterns and avoid aggressive eviction until the autoscaler confirms sustained pressure (targeted for tomorrow’s hotfix window).

Attached: kv-eviction-logs-0411.txt (snapshots annotated with trace ids), incident-graph-20270411.png. I’ve also added a temporary trace retention slice for your API key in ticket 76234 so you can pull the full traces.

If you want us to replay any specific job IDs we can do that on your behalf and provide the outputs from both primary and fallback variants for comparison. Let me know job ids or ranges.

We’ll follow up with a postmortem (eta 72 hours) and a recommended compensating config for clients to reduce prefix churn sensitivity.

— Marcus
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Alex, we’ll send a formal postmortem and the credit proposal within 72 hours. Marcus will coordinate a short executive recap call after the postmortem.

— Marcus
